blocks.text: Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser is available as a native mobile application for iOS, iPadOS, and Android.

On a personal or corporate phone or tablet, the Enterprise Browser mobile app provides a governed workspace that enforces policy, prevents data loss, and protects users from everyday browser-based threats.
The following table describes the key features and capabilities of the app:

table: Applies URL, category, and content policy to every page a user opens, and inspects the page as it renders for browser-borne threats such as phishing and fake login pages or malicious QR codes. Unauthorized or unsafe pages are blocked or accompanied by a warning, the policy rule that was triggered is recorded, and users can raise a time-boxed exception request for administrator review.

Governs copy and paste at the browser boundary. Copying from a managed application, pasting into an unsanctioned site, and moving content into a personal application on the same device are each subject to policy, and clipboard activity is recorded for investigation.

Controls files moving in both directions. Uploads to unsanctioned storage services and uploads from the camera roll or device storage can be blocked or restricted to approved destinations, downloads can be restricted where the mobile platform allows it, and browser-based file transfers are recorded.
Inspects what users type or submit into web forms and applies the policy outcome, which can allow, warn, block, or mask the content, so that sensitive values are not exposed to an untrusted page.

Places guardrails around AI use inside the browser. Prompt content, file uploads to AI services, and clipboard transfers into AI tools are all subject to policy, so that users can keep using these tools without exposing sensitive data to them.

Restricts printing from sensitive applications and watermarks browser sessions for improved accountability and traceability. The watermark identifies the signed-in user, which deters photography and resharing.
Evaluates device posture before a protected application is opened, and restricts screen capture and screen recording inside the app so that on-screen content cannot be exfiltrated from the device.
